_comment: Each command falls back to an empty allow-decision when the script is MISSING **or BROKEN**. preToolUse hooks fail CLOSED on error, so a hook that raises denies EVERY tool call - and a broken guard blocks its own repair. Measured twice: 2026-08-02 a deleted script (recoverable only by restarting the CLI, which is why Test-Path was added) and 2026-08-03 a script that existed but raised NameError mid-edit, which Test-Path did NOT catch and a restart would NOT have fixed - a human had to edit the file by hand. Existence is not validity, so the guard now also requires a zero exit AND non-empty output. Failing OPEN on a crash is the correct trade here: the ACL is the enforcement, this hook is only the explanation layer, so a crashed hook protects nothing (the kernel still refuses every write) while blocking everything.

preToolUse.powershell: if (Test-Path scripts/hooks/credential_gate.py) { $o = python scripts/hooks/credential_gate.py 2>$null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $o) { $o } else { '{}' } } else { '{}' }
preToolUse.bash: if [ -f scripts/hooks/credential_gate.py ]; then o=$(python scripts/hooks/credential_gate.py 2>/dev/null); if [ $? -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$o" ]; then echo "$o"; else echo '{}'; fi; else echo '{}'; fi
